q: Which practice loosens and aerates the soil?
solution: Ploughing turns and loosens the soil.

q: Fertilisers are mainly:
solution: They are concentrated mineral nutrients, usually N, P and K.

q: Why should weeds be removed from a crop field?
solution: Weeds compete with crops for water, nutrients, light and space, reducing yield.

q: Which method saves the most irrigation water?
solution: Drip irrigation delivers water directly to the root zone.

q: Grain should be stored after:
solution: Dry grain resists mould and pests.

q: Name two modern irrigation methods.
solution: Drip irrigation and sprinkler irrigation.

q: Which microorganism turns milk into curd?
solution: Lactobacillus bacteria produce lactic acid.

q: Antibiotics are used to treat:
solution: Antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses.

q: Name two useful products made with the help of microorganisms.
solution: Curd (Lactobacillus) and bread (yeast); also antibiotics and biogas.

q: Malaria is caused by a:
solution: Plasmodium, a protozoan, causes malaria, spread by Anopheles mosquitoes.

q: Which food preservation method removes water?
solution: Drying removes water that microorganisms need to grow.

q: Name two ways to prevent the spread of communicable diseases.
solution: Vaccination and safe drinking water (also handwashing and vector control).

q: Rayon is made from:
solution: Rayon is a semisynthetic fibre derived from cellulose in wood pulp.

q: Which synthetic fibre is strongest and most elastic for ropes?
solution: Nylon has high tensile strength and elasticity.

q: Why are synthetic clothes uncomfortable in summer?
solution: They do not absorb sweat readily, so moisture stays trapped against the skin.

q: Which plastic cannot be softened and remoulded?
solution: Thermosetting plastics such as bakelite degrade rather than melt.

q: Why is plastic a pollution problem?
solution: Microorganisms cannot break it down, so it accumulates.

q: Distinguish thermoplastics from thermosetting plastics with one example each.
solution: Thermoplastics soften on heating and can be remoulded (polythene); thermosetting plastics cannot (bakelite).

q: Which of these is a non-metal?
solution: Sulphur is a non-metal, brittle and a poor conductor.

q: Metals react with dilute acids to produce:
solution: Hydrogen gas is displaced from the acid.

q: Why is sodium kept immersed in kerosene?
solution: It is so reactive that it catches fire in air; kerosene keeps out air and moisture.

q: Which metal is used for electrical wiring because of good conductivity?
solution: Copper conducts electricity and is ductile enough to draw into wire.

q: Stainless steel is an alloy of:
solution: Chromium and nickel improve strength and rust resistance.

q: Give one use each of oxygen and nitrogen.
solution: Oxygen: respiration and medical support; nitrogen: fertilisers and food packaging.

q: Which resource is exhaustible?
solution: Coal is finite and cannot be replenished on human timescales.

q: Petroleum is refined by:
solution: Fractions separate by boiling point in a fractionating column.

q: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
solution: They formed over millions of years and are being used much faster than they form.

q: Which energy source is renewable?
solution: Sunlight is continuously available.

q: Recycling aluminium saves mainly:
solution: Recycling aluminium uses far less energy than extracting it from ore.

q: State two ways to reduce consumption of petrol.
solution: Use public transport and maintain properly inflated tyres (or cycle for short trips).

q: Which is required for combustion?
solution: Oxygen supports combustion.

q: The hottest part of a candle flame is the:
solution: The outer zone has the most complete combustion.

q: Name two ways to extinguish a fire.
solution: Cut off the oxygen supply and remove the heat (cool it).

q: The unit of calorific value is:
solution: Calorific value is energy released per kilogram.

q: Acid rain is mainly caused by:
solution: These oxides dissolve in rain water to form acids.

q: What is a good fuel?
solution: A fuel that has high calorific value, low pollution, and is cheap and easy to store and transport.

q: Clearing of forests is called:
solution: Deforestation is the removal of forest cover.

q: Animals found only in a specific area are called:
solution: Endemic species are restricted to a specific region.

q: State two consequences of deforestation.
solution: Habitat loss and increased soil erosion and floods.

q: Which law protects wildlife in India?
solution: The Wildlife Protection Act provides legal protection to wildlife.

q: Project Tiger was launched to:
solution: It conserves tiger populations and their ecosystems.

q: Differentiate a national park from a wildlife sanctuary.
solution: A national park conserves the whole ecosystem; a sanctuary mainly protects specific species and allows some regulated activities.

q: The control centre of the cell is the:
solution: The nucleus contains the genetic material that directs cell activity.

q: Which structure is present in plant cells but not in animal cells?
solution: The cellulose cell wall gives plants shape and rigidity.

q: Why is the cell called the structural and functional unit of life?
solution: It is the smallest unit that can carry out all life processes and makes up all living things.

q: Mitosis is used for:
solution: Mitosis produces identical daughter cells.

q: A group of similar cells performing a specific function is a:
solution: Tissues are groups of similar cells.

q: Arrange in order of organisation: organ, cell, organ system, tissue.
solution: Cell -> tissue -> organ -> organ system.

topic: Sexual and Asexual Reproduction in Animals
q: Fertilisation in frogs is:
solution: Eggs and sperm meet in water.

topic: Sexual and Asexual Reproduction in Animals
q: Animals that give birth to young are called:
solution: Viviparous animals develop the embryo inside the mother.

topic: Sexual and Asexual Reproduction in Animals
q: Why is sexual reproduction advantageous to a species?
solution: It produces genetic variation, helping the population adapt to changing conditions.

q: The change from larva to adult is called:
solution: Metamorphosis is a dramatic change in body form.

q: A tadpole breathes using:
solution: Tadpoles have gills for aquatic life.

q: What is the function of the placenta?
solution: It allows exchange of oxygen, nutrients and wastes between the mother and the developing embryo.

q: The period between childhood and adulthood is called:
solution: Adolescence is the transition to adulthood.

q: Which hormone helps bring about male secondary sexual characteristics?
solution: Testosterone is produced in the testes.

q: Define puberty.
solution: The stage when the body becomes capable of reproduction, marked by physical changes controlled by hormones.

q: Reproductive health includes:
solution: It covers overall well-being related to reproduction.

q: During menstruation, it is important to:
solution: Cleanliness prevents infection and discomfort.

q: Name two habits that support adolescent health.
solution: Balanced diet and adequate sleep (also exercise and hygiene).

q: Which is a non-contact force?
solution: Magnetic force acts without touching.

q: Force is measured in:
solution: The SI unit of force is the newton.

q: State two effects a force can have on an object.
solution: It can change the object's shape and change its speed or direction of motion.

topic: Pressure in Solids, Liquids and Gases
q: Pressure is:
solution: Pressure is force per unit area.

topic: Pressure in Solids, Liquids and Gases
q: Liquid pressure ______ with depth.
solution: More liquid above means more weight pressing down.

topic: Pressure in Solids, Liquids and Gases
q: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?
solution: It has a smaller area of contact, so the same force produces greater pressure.

q: The friction that acts when a body rolls is:
solution: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction.

q: Friction can be reduced by:
solution: Lubricants create a thin layer that separates surfaces.

q: Give two examples where friction is useful.
solution: Walking on the ground and writing with a pen (also braking a bicycle).

q: Treaded tyres are used to:
solution: Treads push water away and improve grip on wet roads.

q: Streamlining reduces:
solution: A streamlined shape lets air or water flow smoothly around an object.

q: Why is friction called a necessary evil?
solution: It causes wear and wastes energy, but without it we could not walk, hold objects or stop vehicles.

q: Sound cannot travel through:
solution: A vacuum has no particles to carry the vibration.

q: Sound travels fastest in:
solution: Particles in solids are closest, so vibrations pass quickly.

q: Why can you hear the sound of a distant train through rails before hearing it in air?
solution: Sound travels much faster through steel than through air.

q: Pitch depends on:
solution: Higher frequency gives higher pitch.

q: Loudness depends on:
solution: Larger amplitude means louder sound.

q: State two ways to reduce noise pollution.
solution: Use silencers on vehicles and grow tree belts (also use sound-absorbing material).

q: Which liquid conducts electricity best?
solution: Dissolved salts provide ions that carry current.

q: Electroplating uses:
solution: Metal ions are deposited by electric current.

q: Why does distilled water not conduct electricity while tap water does?
solution: Tap water contains dissolved salts that provide ions; distilled water has almost no ions.

q: Pure copper is obtained by:
solution: Ions of copper deposit on the cathode, leaving impurities behind.

q: Electroplating is used to:
solution: A thin metal coating protects and beautifies the object.

q: Name two industries that use electrolysis.
solution: Metal refining and electroplating (also chlorine manufacture).

q: Lightning is caused by:
solution: Charge separation in clouds leads to a huge discharge.

q: A lightning conductor works by:
solution: It provides a low-resistance path to the ground.

q: Why does thunder follow lightning?
solution: Light reaches us almost instantly, while sound takes about 3 s per km, so thunder is heard later.

q: Earthquakes are measured on the:
solution: Magnitude is measured on the Richter scale.

q: Earthquakes are most common at:
solution: Most earthquakes occur where tectonic plates meet.

q: What should you do during an earthquake?
solution: Drop, cover under a sturdy table and hold on; stay away from windows and heavy objects.

q: Bending of light when it changes medium is:
solution: Refraction is the change in direction due to a change in speed.

q: The image in a plane mirror is:
solution: Plane mirrors give upright virtual images.

q: State the two laws of reflection.
solution: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection; incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.

q: Myopia is corrected by a:
solution: A concave lens diverges light so the image falls on the retina.

q: The structure that controls the amount of light entering the eye is the:
solution: The iris adjusts the size of the pupil.

q: What is the function of the retina?
solution: It contains light-sensitive cells that convert light into electrical signals sent to the brain.

q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
solution: Mercury is the innermost planet.

q: The asteroid belt lies between:
solution: Most asteroids orbit in the gap between Mars and Jupiter.

q: Why is Earth the only planet known to support life?
solution: It has liquid water, a suitable atmosphere and a moderate temperature range.

q: A light year is a unit of:
solution: It is the distance light travels in one year.

q: Our nearest star is:
solution: The Sun is the closest star to Earth.

q: What is a constellation? Give one example.
solution: A group of stars that appears to form a pattern; for example Ursa Major.

q: Which gas causes acid rain?
solution: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides dissolve in rain to form acids.

q: CFCs harm the:
solution: Chlorofluorocarbons break down ozone molecules.

q: Name three sources of air pollution.
solution: Vehicles, factories and burning of fossil fuels (also dust and biomass burning).

q: Eutrophication is caused by:
solution: Nutrient enrichment causes excessive algal growth.

q: Which is a waterborne disease?
solution: Cholera spreads through contaminated water.

q: State two ways to reduce water pollution.
solution: Treat sewage before release and avoid dumping industrial chemicals and plastic into water bodies.
